旧.meaning: When the town gets bright new street lamps, the old paper <part>sun</part> from the school play is nailed to a <part>pole</part> in the square. Every evening the grandpas gather under it, squinting fondly at its peeling paint and talking about the <kanji>old times</kanji>.
旧.on: They argue over who was best at pool, waving a chipped <sound>cue</sound> at the paper sun.
旧.kun: One snoozes on a <sound>fu</sound>ton under the pole while a <sound>roo</sound>k pecks at the peeling paint.

揺.meaning: In a storm, the ship's cook hangs his lucky <part>can opener</part> from the <part>anchor</part> chain above the galley. Back and forth it goes, like a hypnotist's watch, until the whole crew is snoring in time to its <kanji>swing</kanji>.
揺.on: Only the captain stays awake, doing tricks with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo that dips in time with it.
揺.kun: A <sound>yu</sound>zu rolls from one side of the deck to the other as the ship sways.

詰.meaning: A best man has an hour-long <part>speech</part> and only one tiny <part>good luck</part> card to write it on. He shrinks his handwriting until every word fits, edge to edge, up the sides and round the stamp. The card is <kanji>packed</kanji>.
詰.on: He reads it out through a magnifying glass while a <sound>kit</sound>ten bats at the card.
詰.kun: Then he sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and tiny words fly off the crowded card.

請.meaning: A man painted <part>blue</part> from head to toe stands on a box outside the bakery and gives a <part>speech</part> to every passer-by about saving the town's last duck pond. He holds out his hat after every sentence. He's there to <kanji>solicit</kanji>.
請.on: Each coin he collects goes straight into a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe strapped to his back.
請.kun: At night he counts it all over a steaming bowl of <sound>u</sound>don.

測.meaning: A lifeguard won't open the pool until she knows how deep it is, so she lowers the old school <part>rule</part> on a string, and <part>water drops</part> splash up her arm. Two feet, three feet, then the rule sinks out of sight. She's still trying to <kanji>measure</kanji> the deep end.
測.on: Next she ties a long stripy <sound>sock</sound> to a broom and tries again.
測.kun: She chalks the depth on the door of the lifeguard <sound>hu</sound>t, next to a doodle of a <sound>ca</sound>rp.

威.meaning: A tiny old <part>woman</part> takes over from the castle <part>sentry</part> for one night. She doesn't shout or wave the spear; she just stares at each visitor over her glasses until they say sorry and go home. Nobody can <kanji>intimidate</kanji> like grandma.
威.on: Even an <sound>ee</sound>l in the moat slides away from her glare.
威.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' squeaks a <sound>do</sound>lphin in the moat, and dives out of sight.

頃.meaning: A cook judges time with a <part>spoon</part> and a <part>rubber duck</part>: she drops the duck in the soup and stirs, and when it has sailed round the pot ten times, dinner is roughly ready. Never exact, always <kanji>about</kanji> right.
頃.on: The <sound>ca</sound>ke gets the same test: ten laps of the duck round the batter bowl.
頃.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala and a <sound>ro</sound>dent wait at the table, asking if it's about time yet.

控.meaning: A young balloon pilot longs to float off into the open <part>sky</part>, but his mum has hooked an <part>anchor</part> to the basket. Every time it rises, she reels it back down: 'Not today, it's windy.' He has to <kanji>withdraw</kanji> from the balloon race.
控.on: He sulks in the basket, licking an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne instead.
控.kun: His mum pins the anchor down with one high <sound>hee</sound>l and tosses him a pickled <sound>ca</sound>rp for lunch.

齢.meaning: The queen <part>orders</part> a shy dragon to open wide, and the royal dentist climbs in with a torch. Every <part>tooth</part> has rings like a tree stump, and she counts them one by one: nine hundred and four. The dragon blushes at its <kanji>age</kanji>.
齢.on: A <sound>ray</sound> glides up the moat carrying the birthday cake on its back, all nine hundred and four candles lit.
齢.kun: The dragon's favourite treat is a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt with <sound>wa</sound>sabi and an <sound>ee</sound>l on top.

審.meaning: Under one leaky <part>roof</part>, the farm animals hold court. Each takes a <part>turn</part> to speak while the goat judge chews the evidence, and rain drips on whoever is talking, so everyone talks fast. The hen blames the fox, the fox blames the hen. It's a long <kanji>hearing</kanji>.
審.on: The hen points at a muddy footprint on her <sound>shin</sound> as proof.
審.kun: The goat sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', sips from a <sound>mu</sound>g, and fines a <sound>bee</sound>tle by mistake.

廃.meaning: The village's silly laws are kept in one old <part>shed</part>: no whistling, no blue socks. At its <part>departure</part> party, the mayor tows the whole shed to the dump behind a tractor, and every rule inside goes with it. That's how you <kanji>abolish</kanji> a law.
廃.on: Bees from a <sound>hi</sound>ve on the shed's roof wave goodbye as it rattles off.
廃.kun: All that's left is a ring of black <sound>soo</sound>t and a rusty <sound>tu</sound>b nobody misses.

複.meaning: On a cruise ship, a <part>weathervane</part> spins on top of a <part>deck chair</part>, and every time it points at a passenger, an identical chair pops up beside them. By lunch the deck is wall-to-wall chairs, each one a perfect <kanji>duplicate</kanji>.
複.on: The crew hang the spare chairs on a big <sound>hook</sound> off the side of the ship.

岩.meaning: A <part>mountain</part> sneezes in its sleep and a single <part>stone</part> pops out of its peak like a cork. It rolls down, picking up pebbles, gravel and a hiker's lost hat, and by the time it stops at the bottom it's the size of a bus: a <kanji>boulder</kanji>.
岩.on: It's covered in sticky green <sound>gun</sound>k from the mountain's nose.
岩.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l slithers out from under it and licks off the gunk like <sound>wa</sound>sabi.

溶.meaning: An ice sculptor carves a swan and sets it in a glass <part>form</part> to show it off at a wedding. By the speeches, <part>water drops</part> are running down the sides; by the cake, the swan is a puddle in a jar. It was always going to <kanji>melt</kanji>.
溶.on: A kid fishes the last chip of swan out with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo string.
溶.kun: The groom toasts the puddle anyway, then turns to an ice <sound>to</sound>tem pole dripping in the corner.

祭.meaning: The villagers pitch a <part>tent</part> right over the stone <part>altar</part> so rain can't spoil the offerings, then march round it seven times banging pots, with paper fish on their heads. Nobody remembers why, but they do it every spring: it's the <kanji>ritual</kanji>.
祭.on: Afterwards, everyone shares a warm jug of <sound>ci</sound>der inside the tent.
祭.kun: The chief fills a <sound>mu</sound>g, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' all over the offerings.

届.meaning: A tired courier plants a <part>flag</part> on every roof she visits, so she never knocks twice. When a man asks why there's a flag on his chimney, she hands him the <part>reason</part> on a sticky note: 'Your parcel is in the bin.' She will always <kanji>deliver</kanji>.
届.on: Her fastest parcels drop out of the sky from a <sound>ki</sound>te.
届.kun: Today's load: a <sound>to</sound>tem pole for a <sound>do</sound>lphin who lives by the pier.

徒.meaning: The ski <part>chairlift</part> breaks down, so a <part>runner</part> in shorts jogs straight up the slope past all the stuck skiers, waving cheerfully. She's at the top before the engineers arrive. Who needs a lift? She goes everywhere <kanji>on foot</kanji>.
徒.on: At the summit she leans on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole to catch her breath.
徒.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeal the skiers as she flicks a <sound>ta</sound>co and a yu<sound>zu</sound> up at them, cheering '<sound>Rah</sound>!': pure mischief.

均.meaning: The groundskeeper must flatten the lumpy <part>soil</part> before the ice show, so he spreads chips of <part>ice</part> over it, seals it all under a tight plastic <part>wrap</part>, and has the skating team stomp across it. Not one bump is left. The rink is perfectly <kanji>level</kanji>.
均.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher lands on it and skids from end to end without a wobble.
均.kun: The skaters celebrate with warm <sound>na</sound>an and a cheerleader's '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

埋.meaning: A farmer is sick of his creaky <part>farm</part>, so one night he shovels <part>soil</part> over the whole thing: barn, tractor and squeaky gate. Next morning there's only a smooth green hill with one weathervane poking out. He's managed to <kanji>bury</kanji> it.
埋.on: Underneath, a crowd of <sound>mi</sound>ce move into the barn and throw a party.
埋.kun: They feast on cold <sound>u</sound>don from the buried kitchen.

炭.meaning: A dragon sleeps inside a <part>mountain</part> and snores fire all winter. In spring the miners dig in and find nothing but <part>ashes</part> and whole logs baked black and crunchy. They fill their carts and sell it for barbecues: dragon <kanji>charcoal</kanji>.
炭.on: They wheel the carts out through a long, dark <sound>tun</sound>nel.
炭.kun: Covered in <sound>soo</sound>t, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat pops out at the far end, coughing.

飾.meaning: At a pool party, the host lays a striped <part>towel</part> along the <part>diving board</part> and piles it with <part>food</part>: grapes in rows, cheese stars, a jelly whale at the tip. Swimmers bounce off it with mouthfuls. She can never resist the urge to <kanji>decorate</kanji>.
飾.on: She wraps fairy lights round the wet ladder and gets a tingly <sound>shock</sound>.
飾.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the pool shouting 'Huz<sound>zah</sound>!' at the jelly whale.

託.meaning: Before her holiday, a singer leaves her lucky coat on a <part>hanger</part> at the dry cleaner's and gives it a long <part>speech</part>: 'Be brave, stay fresh, I'll be back in a week.' The cleaner nods and takes the ticket. She has to <kanji>consign</kanji> it to strangers.
託.on: She tips him with a crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co tucked in the coat pocket.
託.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp and a <sound>ko</sound>ala sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' on the coat and claim it as theirs, on a flimsy excuse.

舎.meaning: Lost in a storm, a hiker opens his giant <part>umbrella</part>, plants the handle in the ground and ties a <part>good luck</part> charm to the tip. By morning it has grown walls, a door and a chimney puffing smoke. He's living in a <kanji>cottage</kanji>.
舎.on: A <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock lands on the roof, and he keeps it as a weathervane.
舎.kun: Inside, he knits <sound>ya</sound>rn socks for a <sound>do</sound>lphin who knocks at the door for shelter.

誘.meaning: At the job fair, a smooth recruiter gives a <part>speech</part> promising that everyone who joins will <part>excel</part>: a corner office, free waffles, a pony on Fridays. Students drift towards his stall in a trance. He knows how to <kanji>entice</kanji> them.
誘.on: The pony turns out to be a cardboard <sound>u</sound>nicorn.
誘.kun: And the free waffles are <sound>sa</sound>rdines on a <sound>so</sound>fa cushion.

捕.meaning: A pirate fed up with mosquitoes ties a <part>flyswatter</part> to the ship's <part>anchor</part> and swings it round his head like a lasso. Thwack: he misses every bug but snags a passing seagull's lunch. Still, it's his best <kanji>catch</kanji> all week.
捕.on: The seagull's stolen lunch is a soggy <sound>ho</sound>tdog.
捕.kun: He nails the hotdog to the ship's <sound>to</sound>tem pole as a trophy.

副.meaning: Whenever the queen is away, her <part>cookie jar</part> sits on the throne, and her second-in-command stands beside it with a tiny chocolate <part>dagger</part>, ready to defend every crumb. He's only the <kanji>vice</kanji> queen, but he takes it very seriously.
副.on: At night he hangs the jar on a <sound>hook</sound> above his bed, just in case.

粉.meaning: A fussy chef cuts each grain of <part>rice</part> in half, then each <part>part</part> in half again, and again, all night with a tiny knife. By sunrise the bowl holds a soft white cloud that puffs up when she sneezes. She's made <kanji>flour</kanji>.
粉.on: Then a ty<sound>phoon</sound> blows in through the window and the whole kitchen turns white.
粉.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala wakes up dusted white on a pile of <sound>na</sound>an.

液.meaning: Every <part>night</part>, the moon leaks: silver <part>water drops</part> drip off its edge into a bucket on the roof. By dawn the bucket is full of something cold, glowing and wobbly. Nobody knows what it is, only that it's a <kanji>fluid</kanji>.
液.on: An <sound>ech</sound>idna sips it through a straw and glows all day.

鮮.meaning: At the harbour market, a <part>sheep</part> in a white coat sniffs every <part>fish</part> before it's sold. One whiff of yesterday and she bleats it off the stall. Only one kind of fish gets past her nose: <kanji>fresh</kanji>.
鮮.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands by her stall so nobody sneaks old mackerel back on.
鮮.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps the crowd, then 'Huz<sound>zah</sound>!', as a shining fish flips up into the light.

頂.meaning: In the middle of a busy <part>street</part>, the mayor hands a butler a <part>rubber duck</part>. He balances it on the very top of his head and bows lower and lower without dropping it. That's how a good butler will <kanji>receive</kanji> a gift.
頂.on: Around its neck, the duck wears a tiny pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker.
頂.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeaks the duck as the mayor adds a <sound>ta</sound>co and a real <sound>du</sound>ck to the pile.
